rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.6 and 3.1-3.3 report the authors' own UAV multispectral flights (Phantom 4, NDVI and TCARI/OSAVI maps, Figures 3-4), drying-chamber sensor data (Figure 5) and microbiological plate counts (Figure 6).
rows.notes: The study uses UAV multispectral imagery (no thermal sensor) only to map NDVI and TCARI/OSAVI as proxies of chlorophyll/vigor and to pick the harvest date of rosemary and sage. It reports nothing on water stress, irrigation scheduling, water use or detection of biotic/abiotic constraints. The canopy-vigor/chlorophyll mapping is at most a precondition of the irrigation-scheduling/water-conservation effect claimed, so Q2 is no and upstream is set.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.6 and 3.1-3.3 report own UAV flights, drying sensor data and microbiological analyses. Q2: Section 2.4 and 3.1 (Figure 3): UAV multispectral NDVI and TCARI/OSAVI maps were used to identify the harvest time; rosemary was harvested when most plants had NDVI about 0.64 with flowering confirmed visually, sage when NDVI was about 0.59, on a semi-arid (Csa, xeric) Sicilian farm.
rows.notes: Q2 is a qualified yes limited to the harvest-timing part of the claim: the study applied UAV multispectral mapping to choose harvest dates for two aromatic crops, but it did not combine this with precision irrigation or nutrient management, did not measure water-use efficiency, used no thermal sensor, and did not evaluate the effectiveness of the timing (no yield, quality or comparison data). The visual flowering check is only a casual confirmation, not an independent method establishing the result (Q3 no). The TCARI/OSAVI-chlorophyll relationship is taken from reference [63], not measured here (Q4 no). One farm, two crops, no limitations or dispersion reported (Q5-Q9 no).

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references), with some duplicated lines from PDF layout. The paper is a single-farm case study in Grotte, Sicily combining UAV multispectral mapping (NDVI, TCARI/OSAVI) for harvest timing of rosemary and sage, a photovoltaic-powered smart solar dryer with WSN monitoring, and microbiological assessment before/after drying. It contains no thermal imaging, no irrigation treatments or scheduling, no water-stress or water-use measurements, and no CWSI work, so it offers no own evidence for the irrigation-related claims it is cited for.
